question_text: What is a couple? Give one example.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Two equal and opposite forces whose
lines of action do not coincide form a
steps.why: The net force of a couple is zero, so nothing accelerates in a line — but the torques add, so the body turns. That split is the definition.
common_mistakes: Calling any two opposite forces a couple — their lines of action must be SEPARATED.

recall.must_convey: That a couple is two equal, opposite, separated forces producing pure rotation.
accept: equal and opposite forces not in the same line

steps.memory_tip: Three conditions: equal, opposite, and lines of action SEPARATED. All three are needed.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition plus the phrase "rotation without translation".

steps.label: The example

lines.text: Example: turning a tap, winding a
clock key, opening a bottle cap.

steps.why: Every two-finger twist in daily life is a couple; one example is enough for the mark.
common_mistakes: Giving a single-force example such as pushing a door.

recall.must_convey: That turning a tap or winding a key is a couple.
reject: equal and opposite forces not in the same line

steps.memory_tip: One finger cannot make a couple. A single force is a torque, not a couple.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. One example is enough — name it and stop.

insider_note: The example is the second mark, not an extra. Turning a tap is enough — one named example, one line.
